[0] At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ outperformed rivals like HBO to become the most awarded platform of the night. Below is HBO's Casey Bloys' response to Apple TV+'s victory.

[1] The HBO CEO praised Apple TV+'s outstanding performance while also acknowledging that competing with a trillion-dollar company is "quite challenging".

[2] Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, with both valuing quality over quantity. Apple has even occasionally been dubbed the "new HBO".

[3] Last night's Emmy Awards further cemented this notion, as Apple TV+ surpassed HBO, Netflix and other platforms to become the most awarded platform of the night.

[4] Apple TV+ took home a total of 29 awards, earning the honour of "most awarded network of the year", with shows like *Widow's Bay* particularly standing out. HBO came in second with 21 awards.

[5] Following the Emmy Awards ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys spoke with Deadline and was asked for his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. Here's what he had to say:

[6] DEADLINE: What are your thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance this time around? They became the most awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time — any comments? BLOYS: I'm actually quite happy about it, because I think they're a very strong competitor — Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong competitors — Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon — so having Apple around keeps everyone on their toes, and that's actually when I perform at my best. They're a trillion-dollar company, and that is indeed quite challenging, but we'll keep doing what we've always done, which is making the best shows out there.

[7] Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has headed programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s win was largely gracious, offering sincere congratulations.

[8] However, the most interesting part of his response was this remark: "They're a trillion-dollar company, and that is indeed quite challenging."

[9] We don't know Apple TV+'s internal budget, but there's no question that Apple's overall financial resources far exceed those of most competitors, including HBO.

[10] Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively pursuing an acquisition of HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

[11] Does scale naturally bring advantages? Perhaps. But many networks have already proven that when it comes to producing content audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

[12] Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, and is also available as part of the Apple One subscription bundle.
